definition: The force acting perpendicular to a surface divided by the area it acts on, $P = \frac{F}{A}$, measured in pascals ($\pu{1 Pa} = \pu{1 N m-2}$).
The number of particles in a sample counted in moles, $n = \frac{N}{N_\text{A}}$, where $N$ is the number of particles and $N_\text{A}$ the Avogadro constant.
The SI unit of amount of substance (mol): one mole of a substance contains $N_\text{A} = 6.02 \times 10^{23}$ particles.
The number of particles in one mole of any substance, $N_\text{A} = \pu{6.02e23 mol-1}$.

A model gas of point molecules in random motion that exert no forces on each other except during elastic collisions, so it has no intermolecular potential energy and, for a fixed amount, obeys $\frac{PV}{T} = \text{constant}$ exactly.
